recipe: Keep components, functions, styles, and state as close as possible to where they are being used to improve readability and reduce redundant re-renders on state updates.
trigger_condition: You are organizing or refactoring a React codebase and want to improve maintainability and performance.
evidence: Keep components, functions, styles, state, etc. as close as possible to where they are being used. This will not only make your codebase more readable and easier to understand but it will also improve your application performance since it will reduce redundant re-renders on state updates.

recipe: If a component contains multiple nested rendering functions, extract each piece of UI that can be considered a unit into its own separate component.
trigger_condition: A component is growing and contains multiple nested rendering functions that make it difficult to maintain.
evidence: Do not add multiple rendering functions inside your application, this gets out of control pretty quickly. What you should do instead is if there is a piece of UI that can be considered as a unit, is to extract it in a separate component.

recipe: Keep your code style consistent across the project and set up linters and code formatters to enforce it.
trigger_condition: You are establishing or reviewing coding conventions for a React project.
evidence: Keep your code style consistent. For example, if you name your components using pascal case, do it everywhere. Most of code consistency is achieved by using linters and code formatters, so make sure you have them set up in your project.

recipe: If a component accepts too many props, split it into multiple components or use the composition technique via children or slots.
trigger_condition: A component is accepting an excessive number of props as input.
evidence: If your component is accepting too many props you might consider splitting it into multiple components or use the composition technique via children or slots.

recipe: Identify repetitions in your codebase before creating shared components, and build a component library around them to improve consistency and maintainability.
trigger_condition: You are working on a larger project with repeated UI patterns and want to create shared abstractions.
evidence: For larger projects, it is a good idea to build abstractions around all the shared components. It makes the application more consistent and easier to maintain. Identify repetitions before creating the components to avoid wrong abstractions.

recipe: Wrap third-party components to adapt them to your application's needs so you can make underlying changes in the future without affecting application functionality.
trigger_condition: You are integrating a third-party component into your React application.
evidence: It is a good idea to wrap 3rd party components as well in order to adapt them to the application's needs. It might be easier to make the underlying changes in the future without affecting the application's functionality.

recipe: Instead of building UI components like modals, tabs, sidebars, or menus from scratch, use an existing battle-tested component library.
trigger_condition: Your project requires standard UI components such as modals, tabs, sidebars, or menus.
evidence: Every project requires some UI components such as modals, tabs, sidebars, menus, etc. Instead of building those from scratch, you might want to use some of the existing, battle-tested component libraries.

recipe: If you have a specific design system to implement, prefer headless component libraries over fully featured ones to avoid the difficulty of adapting pre-styled components.
trigger_condition: You have a specific design system to implement and are choosing between component library types.
evidence: If you have a specific design system to implement, it might be easier and better solution to go with headless components that come unstyled than to adapt a fully featured component library such as Material UI to your needs.

recipe: When choosing a styling solution, keep React Server Components in mind as they require a zero-runtime styling solution.
trigger_condition: You are selecting a CSS or styling approach for a React application that may use Server Components.
evidence: NOTE: Keep React Server Components in mind as they require zero runtime styling solution.
